lab.purpose: Authorized local lab for G0.4c and G1.6a: a lab zone served by an authoritative resolver, a local passive-source stub and four deliberately old service containers, so the discovery chain (names -> addresses -> ports -> services) is reproducible on this host without any internet or external target.

authorization.decision: Leader decision on item 51 (ultron-lead), 2026-11-24, under delegated owner authority: lab = local DNS lab only, in containers on this host; no external targets; third-party passive sources may be queried only for lab/authorized domains, and for the lab zone Subfinder talks to a local stub instead.
authorization.scope: Containers of compose project aegis-lab on this host; internal network aegis-lab-lab (10.114.53.0/24). The zone's passive names use documentation ranges (RFC 5737 203.0.113.0/24, RFC 3849 2001:db8::/32); the service names added in G1.6a resolve to this host's own lab containers inside 10.114.53.0/24. Nothing here resolves or contacts a real host outside this machine, and no scanner runs against a non-lab target.
authorization.evidence: Linear item 51 comment of 2026-11-24; handoff to ultron-pi; report /orca/bots/ultron-lead/memory/reports/g0.4c.md

app.role: lab service on app.lab.aegis.test: Tomcat HTTP 8080 (and AJP 8009), G1.6a

ssh.role: lab service on ssh.lab.aegis.test: sshd on 2222, no credential configured, G1.6a

cache.role: lab service on cache.lab.aegis.test: Redis 6379, no auth (internal network), G1.6a

fingerprintx.role: G1.6b service.fingerprint adapter image, built by make lab-build-fingerprintx (upstream publishes no image)

records.name: txt.lab.aegis.test.
records.value: aegis lab zone; not a real domain

probes.why: A record (MX is not queried by this run)
CNAME to www, resolved in the same answer
outside the lab zone: the resolver is not a forwarder

passive.note: The stub only answers the exact authorized query for the lab zone; it is reached through /etc/hosts inside the run container and a lab-only CA (generated by make lab-up, never committed).

services.note: nginx: HTTPS answers with a certificate from the throwaway lab CA

fingerprint.why: nginx 1.18.0 answers `Server: nginx/1.18.0`; fingerprintx reports the f5 vendor in its CPE, so the parser fills the version into the tool's own vendor/product

services.note: Tomcat: AJP 8009 is open as well; the discovery step only asks for the ports in input. The 404 page prints `Apache Tomcat/9.0.30` in its body, which web.probe_http reads; the AJP port has no provider that identifies it (fingerprintx v1.1.19 has no AJP plugin), so it stays a service with a port state and no product.

fingerprint.why: Tomcat's Server header (`Apache-Coyote/1.1`) carries no product/version the fingerprinter can pin; AJP 8009 has no fingerprintx plugin

services.note: sshd: no credential and no authorized key, banner only

fingerprint.why: banner `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.9`; the SSH identification prefix is not part of the product

services.note: Redis: no auth on the internal network, RDB/AOF disabled. The origin prints `redis_version:6.0.5` for an unauthenticated `INFO server`, but fingerprintx v1.1.19 sends PING only (no INFO, no version), so the chain records protocol `redis` and no product. CVE-2022-0543 is deliberately not expected from a generic redis version: it is a Debian/Ubuntu packaging flaw (Lua sandbox escape in the distro package), not an upstream-Redis version range; when a released fingerprintx extracts INFO, expect upstream-range CVEs instead (e.g. CVE-2021-32626 family).

fingerprint.why: the redis plugin identifies the protocol only; the image's version is not exposed

services.note: Apache 2.4.49: the origin whose product/version the CVE slice matches exactly

fingerprint.why: Apache/2.4.49 (Unix); the tool's CPE is apache:http_server with a `*` version, so the parser keeps its vendor/product and fills the version it read
